question: Following the November 20, 2026 plunge to $103.57 and our Q3 6-K blind-spot audit, what is the verdict for new capital and our 17.764 held Schwab shares?

epigraph.quote: Separate admiration for engineering execution from risk rules on the tape; when a structural stop breaks in Stage 4, cash preservation comes first.
epigraph.author: Dual-Verdict Underwriting Standard

web_blocks.html: SK hynix (NASDAQ: SKHY / KRX: 000660) dominates AI memory with 50%–58% HBM revenue share, ~70% initial HBM4 allocations, and >50% LTA coverage for 2027–2028 capacity, lifting Q3 2026 operating profit to KRW 83.33T (79.7% margin) [2, 13, 15]. Yet our November 2026 Form 6-K audit downgraded KPI health to PASS_WITH_WATCH after revealing 24.87% two-customer concentration, an 83.7% 9M CFO/PAT ratio on KRW 59.12T ending receivables (+KRW 47.44T CFO drag), and a 6.4x jump in unrecognized capex commitments to KRW 42.71T [29]. On November 20, 2026, SKHY plunged 13.11% to $103.57 in a Stage 4 markdown inside a 10-distribution-day US Downtrend, breaching our prior $116.28 structural stop [22]. We assign CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL quality (PASS_WITH_WATCH), REJECTED (TIER_0, TREND, VALUATION) for new capital, and EXIT_IMMEDIATELY on all 17.764 Schwab shares (~$1,839.82) into 100% CASH [22, 29].

First, SKHY sits 5.17 ATRs below a falling $157.01 50-day SMA with 57.47% Bollinger Band width, $10.33–$10.34 daily ATR (9.98% of close), and intraday_4h_turn = false [22]. Third, KRW 59.12T ending receivables (+KRW 47.44T CFO drag) and KRW 42.71T unrecognized capex compress cash quality [29]. Exiting immediately preserves dry powder.

Our rejection tracks price, cash conversion, valuation, and trend rather than pessimism on SK hynix's fabs [22, 29]. To reconsider SKHY, three shifts must appear together [22]. First, shares must stabilize above our derived $81.58–$93.48 monitor band (KRX parity $81.58 to Pivot S2 $93.48 = 158.66 - (186.52 - 121.34)), compress Bollinger Band width below 18%, and reclaim the $157.01 50-day SMA on >=35.5M shares/day [22]. Second, the S&P 500 must exit its 10-distribution-day Downtrend [22]. Third, Q4 2026 results (January 27–28, 2027) must show KRW 59.12T ending receivables collecting into cash without HBM4 margin erosion [28, 29].

Chapters 1 through 6 audit SK hynix blind to stock quotes, integrating the November 16 and November 20 Form 6-K filings across customer concentration, capex commitments, KRW 100T shareholder returns, and Kioxia consolidation [29, 30, 31]. Chapters 7 through 9 then connect those fundamentals to the $103.57 Stage 4 tape, ADR parity, and exact Charles Schwab exit execution [21, 22].

book_paragraphs: Welcome to the refreshed November 20, 2026 institutional monograph on SK hynix Inc., traded on the NASDAQ under SKHY and in Seoul under 000660. Since our November 13 underwriting, both the company's SEC filings and the stock tape shifted dramatically. Two major Form 6-K filings on November 16 and November 20 uncovered critical footnote risks, while the NASDAQ ADR crashed 21.41% in a single week to close at $103.57.

Start with what remains extraordinary inside the business. SK hynix controls 50% to 58% of global High Bandwidth Memory revenue and roughly 70% of initial HBM4 allocations, backed by long-term agreements covering more than half of its 2027 and 2028 production capacity. Nine-month 2026 revenue reached KRW 236.51 trillion, Q3 operating profit hit KRW 83.33 trillion at a 79.7% margin, and liquid cash and short-term investments climbed to KRW 114.46 trillion against KRW 15.80 trillion in debt.

Yet our price-blind Pass 1 audit surfaced four material watch items in the November 2026 filings that forced us to tighten KPI health to PASS_WITH_WATCH. Two unnamed buyers represent 24.87% of 9M 2026 revenue, trade receivables jumped to KRW 59.12 trillion ending balance (+KRW 47.44 trillion CFO working-capital drag, pulling cash conversion down to 83.7%), unrecognized future capex commitments jumped more than sixfold to KRW 42.71 trillion, and $72.13 billion of dollar assets expose pre-tax profit to a KRW 7.22 trillion swing per 10% Korean won move.

Then look at the stock tape on November 20. SKHY tumbled 13.11% on 39.86 million shares to $103.57, tagging a fresh 52-week low of $102.45 and slicing cleanly through our prior $116.28 structural stop loss. Because the NASDAQ ADR has only 95 daily bars since its July 10 debut, the quantitative facts ledger reports insufficient history for a 200-day stage tag, while our snapshot engine classifies SKHY in STAGE_4 (CAP_REJECTED) sitting 34.04% below its $157.01 50-day moving average inside a 10-distribution-day S&P 500 Downtrend.

Our dual verdict reflects strict risk discipline rather than engineering doubt. For new capital, SKHY is REJECTED at TIER_0 due to TREND and VALUATION: even after compressing to 5.77x trailing earnings and 2.55x forward earnings, the ADR trades at a 27.0% premium over Seoul's $580.01 billion ordinary equity value ($81.58 implied parity) and sits above our $73.24 fundamental Base Case, while our Bear-regime stress test yields a -35.7% expected return ($66.59). For our 17.764 held Schwab shares—purchased at $168.88 and now worth $1,839.82—the breach of $116.28 mandates EXIT_IMMEDIATELY, rotating 100% of proceeds into Schwab cash while McKesson and Micron remain at 0%.

book_subsections.title: What Changed Between November 13 and November 20, 2026
paragraphs: Three major developments reshaped our underwriting in seven days. First, the November 16 Q3 Form 6-K exposed the working-capital drag (KRW 47.44 trillion), the KRW 42.71 trillion capex commitment jump, the KRW 122.48 trillion FVTPL asset swings, and the KRW 100 trillion FY2026 shareholder return plan alongside 15-fold SBC growth.

Second, the November 20 Form 6-K confirmed SK hynix will consolidate 100% of SPC2 on December 4, 2026 to hold an indirect ~14.1% stake in Kioxia Holdings. Third, SKHY broke support and crashed through our $116.28 stop to $103.57 while S&P 500 distribution days climbed to ten, forcing an immediate exit on all held shares.

book_subsections.title: How This Monograph Separates Fundamentals From the Tape
paragraphs: Chapters 1 through 6 analyze SK hynix without looking at today's stock quote, testing corporate origins, HBM and Solidigm segments, MR-MUF packaging unit economics, customer and supplier concentration, leading operational dials, and ten-year cash conversion. Chapters 7 through 9 then bring back live market prices, reconciling NASDAQ valuation against Seoul parity, mapping 1W, 1D, and 4H charts, and issuing our Schwab action plan.

book_subsections.title: Key Numbers and Execution Triggers at a Glance
paragraphs: Keep these exact portfolio figures in front of you as you read or listen through the ten chapters. Session close is $103.57; our Schwab position is 17.764 shares ($1,839.82 market value, -$1,160.17 unrealized loss, 2.45% portfolio weight, zero open options); and our action is EXIT_IMMEDIATELY on all 17.764 shares.

Proceeds rotate 100% into Schwab cash (~4.76% 2-year Treasury benchmark), while Shortlist leader McKesson ($1,069.72) and outside memory peer Micron ($594.51, Stage 4) sit at 0%. On the options desk, SKHY rates NO_OPTIONS_EDGE. Our reconciled 12-month fundamental Base Case fair value is $73.24 (a 50/50 blend of $94.34 cycle-peak $50 billion FCF and $52.14 mid-cycle $25 billion FCF) against a $157.01 Bull Case and a $60.06 Bear stress floor at 1.87x KRX P/B (with $81.58 KRX parity along the way).

Keep one overarching principle in mind as you listen to the ten chapters ahead: price-blind fundamental research tells us what a business is worth over a cycle, while Stage 2 tape discipline tells us when it is safe to own it. On November 20, 2026, SK hynix remains a formidable HBM4 leader, yet its broken Stage 4 chart and breached $116.28 stop demand immediate capital preservation. Let us begin in Chapter 1 with the corporate history that forged SK hynix through three decades of memory booms and busts.

Whether you are reviewing this monograph in print or listening to the audio edition, track how every footnote finding in Chapters 3 through 6—the 24.87% customer concentration, the KRW 59.12 trillion trade-receivables build, the KRW 42.71 trillion capex commitment, and the KRW 100 trillion return plan—feeds directly into our valuation and risk decision at $103.57.

Every figure in this dossier is anchored to the verified November 20, 2026 market session, primary SEC Form 6-K filings, live TradingView and Finviz snapshots, and our Charles Schwab account ledger. Let us now walk chapter by chapter through the evidence behind our REJECTED new-capital rating and immediate Schwab exit.
